title: AS2 compiler: global startDrag() has wrong stack order for ActionStartDrag (0x27)
description:
In packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts, the global startDrag() handler pushes arguments in the wrong order for ActionStartDrag (0x27).

Ruffle activation.rs action_start_drag() pops in this order (top = first pop):
  1. target (TOP — popped first)
  2. lock_center
  3. constrain flag
  4. y_max (bottom)
  5. x_max (right)
  6. y_min (top)
  7. x_min (left)  [deepest — popped last]

Current compiler code for startDrag(target, lockCenter, left, top, right, bottom):
  push target first  → deepest  (WRONG: should be TOP)
  push lockCenter
  push constrain=1
  push bottom/y_max
  push right/x_max
  push top/y_min
  push left/x_min    → TOP (WRONG: should be deepest)

This means Ruffle receives: target=x_min, lockCenter=y_min, constrain=x_max, y_max=y_max (partially right?), etc. — all arguments are misread.

All three forms are affected:
- 0-arg: push '', 0, 0 → Ruffle reads target=0 (constrain), should read target=''
- 2-arg: push target, lockCenter, 0 → Ruffle reads target=0 (constrain)
- 6-arg: same as above

Fix for 6-arg form: push in reverse of Ruffle pop order:
  push x_min (args[2]) first → deepest
  push y_min (args[3])
  push x_max (args[4])
  push y_max (args[5])
  push constrain=1
  push lockCenter (args[1])
  push target (args[0]) LAST → TOP

Fix for 2-arg form:
  push constrain=0 first → deepest
  push lockCenter (args[1])
  push target (args[0]) LAST → TOP

Fix for 0-arg:
  push constrain=0 first → deepest
  push lockCenter=0
  push '' (target) LAST → TOP

Note: The MC method form mc.startDrag(lockCenter, ...) goes through ActionCallMethod (0x52) and is NOT affected — that path is correct and tested.

File: packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts around lines 2401-2424.
